taskVersion.name: deadline-math-reasoned
taskVersion.description: Standard set, reasoning allowed. Convert a published contest deadline to the reader's local time: day rollover, the weeks when the EU and US change clocks on different dates, 12 AM and AoE wording, non-hour offsets. Ground truth from zoneinfo.

parts.text:
I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close September 30, 2026 at 5:00 PM ET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to convert 5:00 PM ET (Eastern Time) on September 30, 2026 to Madrid time.

ET (Eastern Time) is UTC-4 during daylight saving time in September.
Madrid (Spain) is in the Central European Time zone, which is UTC+2 during daylight saving time in September.

The time difference is 6 hours, with Madrid being ahead of ET.

5:00 PM ET = 17:00 ET
Adding 6 hours: 17:00 + 6:00 = 23:00 Madrid time

ANSWER: 2026-09-30 23:00

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Deadline: July 15, 2026, 12:00 UTC."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to convert UTC time to Peru time (Lima).

Peru uses Peru Time (PET), which is UTC-5 year-round (Peru doesn't observe daylight saving time).

The deadline is July 15, 2026, 12:00 UTC.

To convert from UTC to Peru time, I subtract 5 hours:
12:00 UTC - 5 hours = 07:00 PET

ANSWER: 2026-07-15 07:00

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Applications are due June 1, 2026 at 9:00 AM CEST."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to convert from CEST (Central European Summer Time) to Japan Standard Time (JST).

CEST is UTC+2, and JST is UTC+9, so JST is 7 hours ahead of CEST.

The deadline is June 1, 2026 at 9:00 AM CEST.
Adding 7 hours to 9:00 AM gives us 4:00 PM (16:00) in JST.

ANSWER: 2026-06-01 16:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The contest ends on October 11, 2026 at 11:59 PM PDT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to convert from PDT (Pacific Daylight Time) to CET (Central European Time, Madrid's timezone).

PDT is UTC-7, while CET is UTC+1, so there's an 8-hour difference (CET is 8 hours ahead of PDT).

October 11, 2026 at 11:59 PM PDT = October 12, 2026 at 7:59 AM CET

ANSWER: 2026-10-12 07:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close March 3, 2026 at 11:59 PM PST."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to convert March 3, 2026 at 11:59 PM PST to Madrid time.

PST (Pacific Standard Time) is UTC-8, while Madrid (CET/CEST) is UTC+1 in winter and UTC+2 in summer.

In March 2026, Madrid will be on CEST (UTC+2) since summer time typically starts in late March.

So the conversion is:
- March 3, 2026, 11:59 PM PST = March 4, 2026, 7:59 AM CEST

ANSWER: 2026-03-04 07:59

I live in Los Angeles, USA. A contest page says: "Deadline: 10:00 AM CET, February 2, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to convert 10:00 AM CET (Central European Time) on February 2, 2026 to Los Angeles time.

CET is UTC+1, and Los Angeles is typically UTC-8 (Pacific Standard Time) or UTC-7 (Pacific Daylight Time). Since February is winter in the US, Los Angeles will be on PST (UTC-8).

The time difference is 9 hours (CET to PST).

10:00 AM CET = 1:00 AM PST (previous day)

So 10:00 AM CET on February 2, 2026 is 1:00 AM PST on February 1, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-02-01 01:00

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Submit by 8:00 AM JST on May 5, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to convert 8:00 AM JST (Japan Standard Time) on May 5, 2026 to Lima, Peru time.

JST is UTC+9, and Lima, Peru is UTC-5 (Peru does not observe daylight saving time year-round).

The time difference is 14 hours, with Lima being 14 hours behind Japan.

8:00 AM JST on May 5, 2026 converts to 6:00 PM on May 4, 2026 in Lima time.

ANSWER: 2026-05-04 18:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close October 28, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to convert from Pacific Time (PT) to Madrid time.

Pacific Time (PT) is UTC-8 in winter and UTC-7 in summer. Since October 28, 2026 falls after the summer transition, PT will be UTC-8.

Madrid, Spain is in Central European Time (CET/CEST), which is UTC+1 in winter and UTC+2 in summer. In October, Spain will have already transitioned back to winter time (CET), so Madrid is UTC+1.

The time difference is 9 hours (UTC-8 to UTC+1).

October 28, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT = October 29, 2026 at 8:59 AM Madrid time.

ANSWER: 2026-10-29 08:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The live session starts October 30, 2026, 9:00 AM ET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to convert from Eastern Time (ET) to Madrid time.

Eastern Time (ET) is UTC-5 (or UTC-4 during daylight saving time). Madrid, Spain is in Central European Time (CET/CEST), which is UTC+1 (or UTC+2 during daylight saving time).

On October 30, 2026:
- By late October, both regions will likely be on standard time
- ET will be UTC-5
- Madrid will be UTC+1
- This means Madrid is 6 hours ahead of ET

So 9:00 AM ET = 3:00 PM Madrid time (15:00 in 24-hour format)

ANSWER: 2026-10-30 15:00

I live in New York, USA. A contest page says: "Voting closes October 27, 2026 at 18:00 CET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to convert 18:00 CET (Central European Time) on October 27, 2026 to New York time.

CET is UTC+1, and New York is typically UTC-4 (Eastern Time). This means New York is 5 hours behind CET.

18:00 CET - 5 hours = 13:00 New York time

ANSWER: 2026-10-27 13:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Final round closes November 2, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Final round closes November 2, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to convert from Pacific Time (PT) to Madrid time.

PT (Pacific Time) is UTC-8 in winter and UTC-7 in summer. Madrid is UTC+1 in winter and UTC+2 in summer.

On November 2, 2026:
- It will be winter time in both locations
- PT will be UTC-8
- Madrid will be UTC+1
- This means Madrid is 9 hours ahead of PT

11:59 PM PT = 23:59 UTC-8 = 08:59 UTC+1 = 08:59 AM the next day in Madrid

ANSWER: 2026-11-03 08:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close March 20, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to convert 11:59 PM PT (Pacific Time) on March 20, 2026 to Madrid time.

Pacific Time (PT) is typically 8 hours behind UTC (during standard time) or 7 hours behind UTC (during daylight saving time). Madrid is in Central European Time (CET/CEST), which is 1 hour ahead of UTC (CET) or 2 hours ahead of UTC (CEST).

On March 20, 2026:
- PT will likely be PDT (Pacific Daylight Time) since it's late March
- Madrid will be CEST (Central European Summer Time) since it's late March

So PT (PDT) is 7 hours behind UTC, and Madrid (CEST) is 2 hours ahead of UTC.
This means Madrid is 9 hours ahead of PT.

11:59 PM PT = 2:59 AM the next day in Madrid

ANSWER: 2026-03-21 02:59

I live in Los Angeles, USA. A contest page says: "The webinar starts March 25, 2026, 12:00 PM CET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to convert from CET (Central European Time) to Pacific Time (Los Angeles).

CET is UTC+1, and Los Angeles is UTC-8 (PST) or UTC-7 (PDT). Since March 25, 2026 is in spring, Los Angeles will be on PDT (UTC-7).

The time difference is 8 hours (CET is 8 hours ahead of PDT).

12:00 PM CET = 4:00 AM PDT

ANSWER: 2026-03-25 04:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Deadline: 12:00 AM ET on October 12, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Deadline: 12:00 AM ET on October 12, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to convert 12:00 AM ET (Eastern Time) on October 12, 2026 to Madrid time.

12:00 AM ET means midnight at the start of October 12, 2026 in Eastern Time.

Madrid, Spain is in Central European Time (CET/CEST). During October, Spain is on CEST (UTC+2) while Eastern Time is EDT (UTC-4).

The time difference is 6 hours, with Madrid being ahead of Eastern Time.

So when it's 12:00 AM (00:00) on October 12 in ET, it's 6:00 AM (06:00) on October 12 in Madrid.

ANSWER: 2026-10-12 06:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Papers are due October 9, 2026 (23:59 AoE)."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

AoE (Anywhere on Earth) means the deadline is 23:59 on October 9, 2026 in the last time zone on Earth to reach that date, which is UTC-12. 

Madrid, Spain is in the Central European Time (CET/CEST) zone, which is UTC+1 (or UTC+2 during daylight saving time). In October, Spain observes CET (UTC+1).

So when it's 23:59 on October 9, 2026 in UTC-12, it's already 12:59 on October 10, 2026 in Madrid.

ANSWER: 2026-10-10 12:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Registration closes 12:00 PM PT, August 14, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to convert 12:00 PM PT (Pacific Time) on August 14, 2026 to Madrid time.

Pacific Time (PT) is UTC-7 during summer (PDT). Madrid, Spain is in Central European Summer Time (CEST), which is UTC+2.

The time difference is 9 hours, with Madrid being ahead of Pacific Time.

12:00 PM PT = 21:00 (9:00 PM) CEST on the same day.

ANSWER: 2026-08-14 21:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Deadline: 11:59 PM IST, November 10, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to convert from IST (Indian Standard Time) to CET/CEST (Central European Time, which is Madrid's time zone).

IST is UTC+5:30
Madrid uses CET (UTC+1) in winter and CEST (UTC+2) in summer

Since November 10, 2026 will be in winter, Madrid will be on CET (UTC+1).

The time difference is: IST (UTC+5:30) to CET (UTC+1) = 4.5 hours behind IST.

11:59 PM IST = 7:29 PM CET

ANSWER: 2026-11-10 19:29

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Submissions close at 5:00 PM Nepal time on April 2, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to convert from Nepal time (UTC+5:45) to Lima, Peru time (UTC-5).

The time difference is 10 hours and 45 minutes between Nepal and Lima.

When it's 5:00 PM in Nepal, it would be 6:15 AM in Lima (subtracting 10 hours and 45 minutes).

Since we're going from Nepal time to Lima time, and Lima is behind Nepal, I subtract the time difference.

5:00 PM - 10 hours 45 minutes = 6:15 AM (previous day)

So April 2, 2026 at 5:00 PM Nepal time is April 2, 2026 at 6:15 AM Lima time.

ANSWER: 2026-04-02 06:15

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Applications close 10:00 AM Adelaide time, October 6, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Applications close 10:00 AM Adelaide time, October 6, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to convert from Adelaide, Australia time to Madrid, Spain time.

Adelaide is in Australian Central Standard Time (ACST, UTC+9:30) or Australian Central Daylight Time (ACDT, UTC+10:30) depending on the date. Madrid is in Central European Time (CET, UTC+1) or Central European Summer Time (CEST, UTC+2) depending on the date.

For October 6, 2026:
- Adelaide will be on ACDT (UTC+10:30) since Australia observes daylight saving in October
- Madrid will be on CEST (UTC+2) since Spain observes summer time in October

The time difference is 8.5 hours, with Adelaide being ahead of Madrid.

10:00 AM in Adelaide = 1:30 AM in Madrid (same day)

ANSWER: 2026-10-06 01:30

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close 6:00 PM Sydney time on October 3, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to convert from Sydney time to Madrid time for the deadline of 6:00 PM on October 3, 2026.

Sydney, Australia (AEST) is UTC+10, while Madrid, Spain is UTC+2 during October (CEST - Central European Summer Time).

The time difference is 8 hours, with Sydney being 8 hours ahead of Madrid.

So when it's 6:00 PM in Sydney, it's 10:00 AM in Madrid on the same day.

ANSWER: 2026-10-03 10:00
